question: Recent reporting by Investigate Europe1 and partner media2 has raised concerns about the appearance of impartiality at the Court of Justice of the European Union, including declared financial interests of Members of the Court and situations where judges may sit in cases involving the Member State that nominated them.

Given that judges and advocates general are appointed, by common accord, by the governments of the Member States after consulting the panel set up under Article 255 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU): 1.

Does the Council consider that the current appointment and reappointment procedure adequately examines candidates’ financial interests, previous governmental functions, and links to the nominating Member State?
Has the Council discussed asking the panel set up under Article 255 TFEU to assess perceived conflicts of interest more systematically before appointments or reappointments?
Will the Council consider publishing clearer safeguards on how perceived conflicts identified during the appointment process are assessed, while fully respecting judicial independence?
